messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — starting a targeted bring-up for model v3q-int4 on 10% of sessions in prod-us-east at 12:15 PT. Primary goal: see concordance + latency tradeoffs on long-context prompts. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Scheduled rollout: v3q-int4 -> 10% sessions (session-hash routes 0-9). Window 30m. Notify @eng-ml on anomalous regressions.

Devon Lee: what's the routing rule again?

Samir Khan: session-hash mod 100 < 10 => goes to canary. We added sticky session routing so users keep same variant.

Irina Voronov: quick ask — do we run both per-token and per-session concordance checks? I think session-level is more stable for code completions.

Maya Patel: yes — most fallback rules are session-level. Per-token metrics still collected for debugging.

Devon Lee: early numbers — p95 latency down 18% on canary so far, throughput +12%. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Samir Khan: nice. Any quality signals?

Devon Lee: aggregated concordance (ranked nLL + token-F1) is -0.9% ABS vs baseline — small but notable. Long-context subset (>512 tokens) shows -3.4% on token-F1.

Irina Voronov: that's the concern. What's our auto-fallback thresholds?

Maya Patel: current rule proposal:
- if session-level concordance delta <= -2.0% absolute AND KL(token distribution) > 0.018 over 30m => immediate per-session fallback
- if global concordance delta <= -1.5% absolute for 60m with p-value < 0.01 => pause traffic expansion and rollback to 5%
- per-customer: if a customer has >1% of their sessions regress by >1.5% for 30m => route all their traffic back to pinned model

Devon Lee: can you add a margin for low-sample slices? e.g., require at least 200 sessions in window.

Maya Patel: yes — sample count >= 200 for global rules, >= 30 for per-customer.

Samir Khan: also propose a quick "partial degrade" step: rather than full rollback, reduce to 2% and enable token-caching override for affected prefixes. That buys time for a hotfix.

Irina Voronov: how do we detect token-distribution shifts robustly? KL is noisy.

Devon Lee: we're using bootstrap on KL with 1000 resamples to get CI, plus a smoothed EWMA on entropy. Alert if 95% CI lower bound > 0.012 and KL point-estimate > 0.02.

Samir Khan: good. Also log example prompts that show largest delta and push to the eval-dashboard automatically.

Maya Patel: deploy-bot has configured the webhook: when any rule fires, it posts thread to #eng-ml with a compact report and attaches top-10 prompt diffs.

deploy-bot: Canary started at 12:15 PT. 10% sessions routed. Metric streams: /dash/canary/v3q-int4

Devon Lee: 12:35 update — sample count 420, global concordance delta -0.6% (p=0.09), long-context sample 48 (too small), p95 latency -15%.

Irina Voronov: Data suggests quality impact concentrated on single intent cluster "multistep-refactor". Can we shadow more from that intent?

Samir Khan: yes — I'm turning on a slice shadow at 100% (no real traffic) for that intent to collect more examples. command:

```
slice-shadow enable --intent multistep-refactor --samples 1000
```

Maya Patel: thanks. Also adding temporary stricter rule: if multistep-refactor slice concordance delta <= -3% over 20m => auto route that intent away from canary immediately.

Devon Lee: okay watchlist active. Early sign: two customers (acct-209, acct-341) show >2% regression on multistep-refactor across recent sessions.

Irina Voronov: @Maya should we proactively fallback those two accounts? They are paying customers.

Maya Patel: yes — per-customer rule applies. Routing acct-209 and acct-341 back now.

deploy-bot: Routing change: acct-209, acct-341 -> baseline model pinned.

Samir Khan: log shows a small tokenization mismatch for a rare marker "/*>>*/" in long prompts — quantization seems to change softmax tail.

Devon Lee: can we add a temporary postprocess that maps that marker to safe tokenization? quick patch in serving:

```
if "/*>>*/" in prompt: prompt = prompt.replace("/*>>*/", " /*>>*/ ")
```

Irina Voronov: ugly but effective for short term.

Maya Patel: patch applied to canary routing for affected sessions. We'll monitor.

Devon Lee: 13:10 update — multistep-refactor slice concordance delta now -1.1% (improved), global delta -0.4%, long-context sample now 210 and delta -1.8%. p-value global 0.03.

Samir Khan: knobs summary:
- sample thresholds enforced
- session-level strict fallback (>=2% & KL>0.018 & samples>=30)
- global pause at -1.5% & p<0.01 & samples>=200
- per-customer immediate fallback if >1% sessions regress >1.5%
- partial-degrade path to 2% traffic

Irina Voronov: do we need an explicit human-in-loop for enterprise accounts? maybe don't auto-fallback for accounts with support_level=enterprise without confirm.

Maya Patel: good catch — update: enterprise customers are excluded from auto-global fallback; per-customer fallback still allowed but requires ops approval if support_level=enterprise. We'll notify SEs.

Devon Lee: can we schedule a quick postmortem doc after the window? want to capture tokenization findings and the patch.

Maya Patel: will create a short postmortem + action items: tokenization unit tests, add "rare-marker" sanitizer, re-run quantization with alternative token-merging.

Samir Khan: ack. TL;DR: keep canary running at 10% for now, blocked customers routed back, add extra shadow sampling on problem intent, apply prompt sanitizer.

Irina Voronov: :thumbsup: Good run — we'll reconvene in 2h or sooner if rules fire.
